- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 73+ → forecast jumps to 75+), then corrects downward.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, missing gradual drifts.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the middle of the horizon, especially when prices are falling from 70–75.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the final 5–10 days, often missing the true price’s upward or downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture the “tail risk” of sudden drops after prolonged stability — underestimates volatility spikes.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 73+), suggesting overconfidence in momentum.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., price dips in March vs. August).
